title: chore: release packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and publish to npm yourself or [setup this action to publish automatically](https://github.com/changesets/action#with-publishing). If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @object-ui/components@18.1.0

### Minor Changes

- 8701f1e: The record page heading draws a `nameField` that declares a widget with a read face of its own through that face, the one the field's list column draws (objectui#13216). A record share (`nameField: 'recipient_id'`, which declares `widget: 'recipient-picker'` and `dependsOn: ['recipient_type']`) now heads its page with the recipient's name instead of the user id it stores. Every other heading is unchanged: a plain text or select `nameField`, a `titleFormat`, an explicit `title`, an object with no `nameField`, a widget with no read face of its own, a widget whose key has no face registered under it (it draws the stored text), and a host that does not load `@object-ui/fields`.
  
  `@object-ui/components` adds a field-face seam on its entry: `setFieldReadFaceResolver(resolver)` installs the resolver, `resolveFieldReadFace(field)` asks it, and the types `FieldReadFace`, `FieldReadFaceProps` and `FieldReadFaceResolver` describe them. `@object-ui/fields` fills it when it loads, with the same `getCellRenderer(resolveCellRendererType(field))` lookup the grid's cells make, so a host has nothing to wire. `RecordTitleChip` gains an optional `titleNode` prop, drawn inside its heading in place of the `title` text; `title` stays a required string.

### Patch Changes

- 7c405b7: A `page:tabs` item whose `visibleWhen` faults on evaluation is no longer drawn (objectui#13286).
  
  A predicate that cannot be evaluated (a source over the CEL engine's AST bound, a type error, an unbound root, a missing function) used to fall back to visible, so the tab drew for a viewer the predicate was written to exclude. It now fails closed: the tab, header and panel, is withheld, and the fault is logged once per authored source through the same console report as before, now saying the tab was withheld. If the withheld tab was the active one, the strip falls back to the first visible tab. A tab with no `visibleWhen`, or a blank one, is still shown, and a predicate that evaluates decides exactly as before. Form field rules keep their documented fail-open.
- fbb4b23: data-table / VirtualGrid: selecting a cell's text no longer opens the record or starts an inline edit, and Ctrl/Cmd+C copies the selected text instead of the whole cell value. A plain click still opens or edits as before (objectui#13188).
- c8f8b10: data-table: with row numbers on, the header's select-all checkbox, each row's checkbox and the row number now share one centre line in the leading column (objectui#13293).

## @object-ui/types@18.1.0

### Minor Changes

- 8556295: `NavigationItemSchema` now refuses a navigation entry whose `visible` reads `data` but which declares no `dataSource`, as `@objectstack/spec`'s `NavigationItemSchema` already does (objectui#13076). The rule is the spec's own exported `navItemVisibleDataNeedsDataSource`, chained on every navigation arm (the flat arm and the `doc` arm), not restated, so `objectui validate` and the platform's save door refuse the same entry with the same issue at `visible`.
  
  This narrows the published validator toward the spec: an entry such as `{ id: 'nav_envs', type: 'object', objectName: 'sys_environment', visible: 'data.total == 1' }` validated clean here and failed at publish; it is now refused here too. Declare the `dataSource` whose bound value `visible` reads, or gate on `current_user` or `features` instead. An entry with a `dataSource`, or whose `visible` is a boolean, absent, or reads no `data`, is unaffected.
## @object-ui/console@18.1.0

### Patch Changes

- a91f6bb: The Approvals Inbox opens a request on the page the platform serves for it, and its side sheet is gone (objectui#12484).
  
  A row, a mobile card, Enter on the focused row, and a notification's `?request=` deep link now open the request's record page: the `sys_approval_request_detail` page `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` serves, on the console's standard record route. That page shows the request's title (the flow's label), its decision panel (the declared amount and snapshot summary, the approvers, the step line and the decisions), its highlights, its target record, and its timeline. The deep link takes its own place in the browser history, so Back returns to where the reader came from; from a row, Back returns to the inbox.
  
  The inbox's own request sheet is deleted. Its quick paths stay: inline approve and reject, bulk decisions, filters, sorting and keyboard navigation.
- 0093b2c: Settings pages: a `url`, `email`, `phone` or `color` value that misses the format its type declares now blocks Save (objectui#13287). No request goes out, the row is marked inline with a message naming what the format expects, and focus moves to the first such row, on the same path as the `required` check. The grammars are the settings service's own (objectstack#24882), judged on the trimmed value; an empty value is left to `required`, and a hidden or env-locked row is not judged. Adds `console.settingsView.invalidPhone` and `console.settingsView.invalidColor` to every locale pack; `email` and `url` reuse `validation.email` and `validation.url`.
- @object-ui/sdui-parser@18.1.0
## @object-ui/app-shell@18.1.0

### Patch Changes

- b001d21: The README's "Setup half of an item" now says what objectstack's shipped organization administrator set does on the assignment objects: it creates and removes rows on `sys_user_position` and `sys_user_permission_set` and never edits them, bounded on the server by the delegated-administration gate, so that administrator sees Add and Remove on a position's and a permission set's holders. No behaviour change.
- 36b70c0: The package edit dialog (Studio / Setup) now edits a package's `dependencies`. The row is no longer locked once the package exists, and saving sends it to `PATCH /api/v1/packages/:id` beside the name, description and version when the author changed it; emptying it sends `{}`, which clears the declaration. The server's `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` for a malformed row and `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` for a read-only package show in the dialog, which stays open.
- 5235d6d: Setup › Packaged automation: the clone result now offers the next steps (objectui#13270).
  
  A clone of a packaged flow is created `draft`, which does not switch it off, so a cloned record-change or schedule flow runs beside the flow it was copied from. The result used to show the server's notice and nothing to click. It now keeps that notice and adds:
  
  - **Switch "SOURCE" off** — calls the same packaged-flow toggle as the row's own switch, for the flow that was cloned. On success the row reads off and the result says the source is switched off. A refusal shows the server's message beside the button, and the button stays. When the source is already off, no switch-off is offered.
  - **Open the clone in Studio** — links the package-less Studio scope (`/studio/~org/automations`) opened on the clone.
  
  The clone itself is unchanged. Three new language-pack keys, `packagedAutomation.cloneSwitchSourceOff`, `.cloneSourceOff` and `.cloneOpen`, in all ten packs.
- cf153eb: The permission-set editor no longer keeps the clone notice once the copy is held or saved (objectui#13272).
  
  "Clone to customize" opens the copy with the server's notice: what was not copied, and that the copy is held by nobody yet. The notice is the server's answer at the moment of the clone. It stayed on the copy for as long as the copy was open, so after a user was assigned and the copy was saved it still said nobody held it. The notice now goes when the copy's Assigned Users list first shows anyone (a direct grant or a holder through a position), or when a save of the copy succeeds. A refused save keeps it, and so does a failed read of the holders. On an embedded host, where the copy is announced on the set it was cloned from, saving that set keeps it too. While the notice shows, it is still shown whole and in the server's words.
- 9e1bff6: The app's report index (`/apps/APP/reports`) and the ⌘K palette's report list now include the reports a module contributes to the app's navigation (`navigationContributions`), not only the reports the app's own package owns. The index lists the union of the app package's reports and every report a `type: 'report'` navigation entry names, deduplicated by name; an entry naming a report the server does not serve is left out, and the dataset read gate still hides a report the member may not read.
- 53dea27: The package dialog's Dependencies row is now an author-facing editor (objectui#13278). It used to be the spec form's raw JSON box under the developer hint "widget object-fields — falling back to JSON until a custom renderer is registered", because the manifest's `dependencies` is a string map the spec form has no renderer for.
  
  The row now lists one line per dependency, a package name and a version range, with add and remove, in create, edit and view mode. It sends the same flat map as before: in edit mode only when changed, and `{}` when every row is removed. An empty or duplicate package name is flagged under its row and keeps save disabled. The ranges are judged by the server, whose refusals render in the dialog as before.
  
  Nothing is added to the package entry: no export, prop or type member. The new copy lives in the metadata-admin designer's own string tables (en and zh).

## @object-ui/fields@18.1.0

### Patch Changes

- 8701f1e: The record page heading draws a `nameField` that declares a widget with a read face of its own through that face, the one the field's list column draws (objectui#13216). A record share (`nameField: 'recipient_id'`, which declares `widget: 'recipient-picker'` and `dependsOn: ['recipient_type']`) now heads its page with the recipient's name instead of the user id it stores. Every other heading is unchanged: a plain text or select `nameField`, a `titleFormat`, an explicit `title`, an object with no `nameField`, a widget with no read face of its own, a widget whose key has no face registered under it (it draws the stored text), and a host that does not load `@object-ui/fields`.

- 8e649da: A row action's `defaultFromRow` param backed by a relation is seeded with the related record's id again, not the whole record (objectui#13271).
  
  Related lists read their rows with the relations they show expanded, so a `lookup`, `master_detail`, `user` or `tree` value arrives as the related record. The param seed copied that record verbatim, and the action sent it where the endpoint expects the id. Setup → Teams → Remove from Team answered 400 "User is not a member of the organization" for every member.
  
  The seed now uses the row's stored form, by the same field-type rule the predicate and Undo paths use: a field the row's object declares relational becomes its id, and a `multiple` one becomes the array of ids. Every other field, including a `json` value that has an `id` key, is seeded exactly as before. The dialog still shows the related record's name. Nothing is added to the package entry.

## @object-ui/plugin-detail@18.1.0

### Patch Changes

- f669732: The inline-edit save bar shows an object-level rule's refusal as the rule's own message, without a field label (objectui#13292).
  
  The server names an object-level rule (a `script` rule, or one that lists no fields) with the `_record` sentinel. The bar used to print that sentinel as a field label, so the banner read `_record: …`. Now an entry that names `_record`, or names no field of the record, is shown alone in the banner and is not published as a per-field hint. Field-level entries are unchanged: they keep their label and their hint beside the input.
